title: Post-SIR, voter base in 5 poll-bound states shrank by up to 13.24 per cent
shows: PTI sets out the rolls of the five states due to vote early next year, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Manipur and Goa, before the revision, at the draft and at the final roll, from figures the Election Commission and the Chief Electoral Officers published. By its count the five rolls fell from about 18.71 crore to 16.43 crore, a fall of about 2.29 crore or 12.2 per cent, and Uttar Pradesh accounts for nearly 90 per cent of it. It gives the fall in the roll as 13.24 per cent in Uttar Pradesh, 10.76 per cent in Goa, 10.07 per cent in Uttarakhand, 6.34 per cent in Punjab and 6.33 per cent in Manipur. For Uttar Pradesh it gives 15.44 crore electors before the revision, 12.56 crore on the draft and 13.40 crore on the final roll, with about 2.89 crore names left off the draft. PTI says about 0.84 crore of those, roughly 29 per cent, were restored, and it describes about 34 per cent in Punjab, about 17 per cent in Manipur and about 3 per cent in Uttarakhand as names that came back. Each of those figures is the rise from the draft to the final roll, which is the names added after the draft, new voters among them, less the names deleted after it, and the report does not say how many of the names added had been left off the draft. Goa's final roll is smaller than its draft.
quote: According to data made public by the Election Commission and state chief electoral officers in recent past, across these five states, the electorate shrank from about 18.71 crore to 16.43 crore after SIR, a net reduction of around 2.29 crore — about 12.2 per cent.
The draft removed about 2.89 crore names, and about 0.84 crore (roughly 29 per cent) were restored.
It had the strongest recovery. About 0.07 crore of the roughly 0.21 crore draft deletions (about 34 per cent) came back to the rolls.
Goa is the only one of the five where the final roll is smaller than the draft, so there was no net restoration.
note: PTI copy, New Delhi, 2 November 2026, as carried by ThePrint (published 2 November 2026, 4:46 pm IST, byline PTI, marked as auto-generated from the PTI feed). ThePrint answered curl with 403, so the full text was read through a scraping service on 3 November 2026. The same copy was read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody of The Tribune's two pages with curl: 'Post-SIR, voter base in 5 poll-bound states shrinks by up to 13%; UP records steepest drop' (datePublished 2026-11-02T17:19:05+05:30, author PTI, isAccessibleForFree true) and a shorter version headed 'Voter base in 5 poll-bound states shrinks by up to 13.24% after SIR' (datePublished 2026-11-03T01:24:46+05:30), which is the headline the owner's screenshot carries. Deccan Herald and The Hindu BusinessLine carry the same copy. Every figure was checked against data/india/states.json and data/india/raw/final.csv. All agree within PTI's rounding. Uttar Pradesh 15,44,30,092 before, 2,88,74,067 left off, draft 12,55,56,025, final 13,39,84,792, fall 2,04,45,300 or 13.24 per cent, rise from draft to final 84,28,767 or 29.2 per cent of those left off. Punjab 2,14,61,043 before, 20,66,635 left off, final 2,01,00,727, fall 6.34 per cent, rise from draft 7,06,292 or 34.2 per cent of those left off, against 7,97,263 added after the draft (2,93,049 of them aged 18 or 19, The Times of India) and 86,038 deleted. Uttarakhand 79,60,762 before, 71,33,785 draft, 71,58,949 final, fall 10.07 per cent, rise from draft 25,164 or 3.0 per cent, against 1,29,872 added and 1,04,708 deleted. Manipur 20,93,076 before, 19,34,399 draft, 19,60,620 final, fall 6.33 per cent, rise from draft 26,221 or 16.5 per cent, which PTI rounds to 17, against 56,871 added and 30,650 deleted. Goa 11,85,034 before, 10,84,992 draft, 10,57,566 final, fall 10.76 per cent, against 12,166 added and 39,592 deleted. The five together go from 18,71,30,007 to 16,42,62,654, a fall of 2,28,67,353 or 12.22 per cent. PTI's words 'restored' and 'came back' describe the net rise from draft to final in every case, and for Uttar Pradesh the Chief Electoral Officer published only the net rise, so the summary says what the figure measures, in the words the site uses for it. The X post by Seema Chishti that shared the report adds her own opinion of the Commission, which is not carried. The report also says the Commission's special summary revision in 17 states gives those left off another chance to enrol, and gives the dates the five assemblies' terms end.
